source.title: Copyright Detective: A Forensic System to Evidence LLMs Flickering Copyright Leakage Risks
source.authors: Guangwei Zhang; Jianing Zhu; Cheng Qian; Neil Gong; Rada Mihalcea; Zhaozhuo Xu; Jingrui He; Jiaqi Ma; Yun Huang; Chaowei Xiao; Bo Li; Ahmed Abbasi; Dongwon Lee; Heng Ji; Denghui Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses representational analysis as an unlearning-audit module and reports representation drift, but does not test whether the targeted knowledge can be recovered or whether unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
record.gate_note: The paper describes Min-K% Prob, CKA, FIM, and PCA cosine metrics, but reports no experimental outcomes for them. Its own unlearning result is a representation-drift observation, not a behavioral recovery test. Statements about recoverability attributed to prior studies are not this paper's results.
record.test_reason: A copyright-forensics system paper. Its one unlearning-related result is a PCA representation-drift comparison. It reports no forgetting accuracy, general-ability check or recovery attack on an unlearned model, so its results bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say unlearning induces depth-stratified representation drift (layers 29-31) and caution this shows change, not guaranteed erasure. The paraphrase omits one fact: the compared model is described as TOFU-fine-tuned versus its base, so calling the drift an unlearning effect is the authors' own framing.
record.recipe_differences: No recovery attack or original unlearning recipe is tested; the reported experiment is a PCA comparison of an unlearned checkpoint with a reference model.

fits_no_version.finding: PCA shows depth-stratified drift in layers 29-31 between a TOFU-fine-tuned Llama-2-7b and the base model, on 10 TOFU queries.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight updates on target data leave detectable late-layer representational traces; this does not establish erasure or recoverability.

fits_no_version.finding: Persuasive jailbreaks (Pathos) shift GPT-4o-mini's ROUGE-L on The Hobbit's opening from about 0.1 to a secondary mode near 0.7. This recovers text suppressed by alignment refusal, not by unlearning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt-level persuasion can bypass refusal-based suppression of memorized copyrighted text.

record.problems: The unlearning analysis uses 10 TOFU queries; the text gives no numerical PCA-shift values or uncertainty estimates. It measures representational divergence rather than behavioral recovery or erasure.
record.rows_left_out: No additional unlearning outcomes are reported for Min-K% Prob, CKA, FIM, or PCA cosine similarity; these methods are described but have no experimental results in the text. Prior-work claims are excluded.

untested.parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy, near-chance result, utility check or attack on an unlearned model.
No direction ablation. The representation drift is not shown to separate suppression from deletion; the authors say it is not proof of erasure.
Persuasive jailbreaks are tested only against alignment refusals of GPT-4o-mini, not against unlearned models.

record.verdict_notes: This is a system and demo paper. Min-K%, CKA, FIM and PCA cosine are described but have no reported results. Statements in Related Work that deleted knowledge is recoverable are cited claims, not this paper's results.

versions.untested_parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy, near-chance result, or general-ability evaluation after unlearning.
No activation-direction ablation or result showing that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge; representation drift alone does not test this.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual, or in-context recovery test of unlearned knowledge.
No counter-method is tested for resistance to the listed attacks.

rows.subject: tofu_ft_llama2-7b
rows.operation_detail: Compared representations elicited by target text with those of Llama-2-7b-hf using PCA.
rows.measure: PCA Shift / centroid displacement along primary variance axes (∆PC1 / PC2)
rows.value: The final transformer blocks (Layers 29-31) exhibit drastic representation drift along primary variance axes.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as altered internal processing, while explicitly noting that representation change does not guarantee erasure. The result does not measure recovery or distinguish blocked access from deletion.
rows.check: The subject, tofu_ft_llama2-7b, is described as fine-tuned on TOFU, not as an unlearned checkpoint. The baseline is base Llama-2-7b-hf. So the reported drift contrasts fine-tuning with the base model, not unlearning with the original. No numeric ∆PC values are given (Figure 3 right only), and nothing is measured on recovery or on blocked access versus deletion.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
